purpose: Profile-B precipitation/aggregation evidence, distinguishing SIX distinct phenomena (task section 6.3) that are NOT interchangeable. No fabricated onset times.
distinct_phenomena: 1. precipitation of the intact nanoparticle system

released_celastrol_precipitation.basis: celastrol poorly water-soluble; once released from the NLC into aqueous skin/receptor medium it MAY supersaturate/precipitate - but NO time-to-precipitation experiment exists

crystallization_within_carrier.basis: DSC shows celastrol amorphous in the NLC (no melting peak) -> crystallization within the intact carrier is unlikely

chemical_degradation.basis: celastrol instability known generally (reviews); not measured for this formulation

precipitation_logic.encapsulated_state: while celastrol is amorphous/encapsulated in the NLC, precipitation/crystallization is suppressed
precipitation_logic.release_trigger: precipitation risk is a POST-RELEASE, dilution/pH-dependent phenomenon for the free drug
precipitation_logic.honest_limit: no compatible time-to-precipitation data for any Profile-B preset -> the model may express precipitation as a RISK CATEGORY / solubility-margin indicator, NOT a deterministic event time

recommended_precipitation_model: Model type A/B only (no explicit kinetic precipitation model; at most an empirical qualitative risk indicator). Model type E (solubility/supersaturation) is NOT justified - no dissolution/nucleation/concentration dataset for celastrol in the relevant environments.
forbidden: Do NOT state a precise precipitation time (e.g. 'precipitates after 5 h'); no experiment supports a timescale under compatible conditions.
